title: The Reachability Engine (Surjectivity)
content: `reach_aux` is the heart of surjectivity. From ANY state `s`, and positive coprime coordinates `(a,b)`, it produces a path whose node is `a·(la,lb) + b·(ra,rb)`. The proof is strong induction on `a+b`: when `a = b`, coprimality forces `a = b = 1` and the empty path already sits at `s`'s mediant; when `a > b` it steps left and recurses on `(a−b, b)`; when `a < b` it steps right and recurses on `(a, b−a)`. This is exactly the subtractive Euclidean algorithm, with `a+b` as the strictly decreasing measure. Notably no determinant hypothesis is needed — the coordinate identities are purely formal.
mathContext: Left step: $a\,(la,lb)+b\,(ra,rb)$ with new ancestors $(la,lb),(la{+}ra,lb{+}rb)$ gives coordinates $(a{-}b,b)$. Right step gives $(a,b{-}a)$. $\gcd(a,b)$ is preserved, so $a=b\Rightarrow a=b=1$.

title: Ancestor Coordinates Linearize the Tree Search
content: The decisive idea is to track the target not as a fraction but as the pair `(a,b)` of weights in `(num,den) = a·(left ancestor) + b·(right ancestor)`. Under this change of variables the geometric tree descent becomes the subtractive Euclid recursion `(a,b) ↦ (a−b,b)` (left) or `(a,b) ↦ (a,b−a)` (right). Because gcd is invariant under subtraction and the target is reduced, the descent can only terminate at `a = b = 1`, which is the node itself. From the root `⟨0,1,1,0⟩` the rational `p/q` has coordinates `(q,p)`, so the measure `a+b` equals the familiar Euclidean quantity `p+q`.

title: Surjectivity onto Coprime Pairs
content: `reach_root` specializes the engine to the tree root: every coprime `(p,q)` with `p,q ≥ 1` is the `(numerator, denominator)` of some Stern-Brocot node. The root state `init = ⟨0,1,1,0⟩` makes the target coordinates simply `(q,p)`, and `pathNum`/`pathDen` read off exactly `p` and `q`. This is the combinatorial core of 'every reduced positive fraction appears in the tree'.

title: Every Positive Rational Is Reached
content: `toRat_surjective` lifts surjectivity from coprime pairs to the rationals: for any `x : ℚ` with `0 < x`, some path satisfies `toRat t = x`. The bridge is Mathlib's rational structure — `Rat.num_pos` gives `x.num > 0`, `Rat.reduced` gives coprimality of `(x.num.natAbs, x.den)`, and `Rat.num_div_den` reassembles `x` from numerator and denominator. Apply `reach_root` to the reduced pair and the path's value is exactly `x`.

title: BST Bounds: Left Below, Right Above the Mediant
content: `left_lt_mediant` and `mediant_lt_right` distill the parent's `value_between_ancestors` into two clean ℕ cross-multiplied facts: a node in `s`'s left subtree has value strictly below `s`'s mediant (`num·(lb+rb) < (la+ra)·den`), and a node in the right subtree strictly above it. Working over ℕ (rather than the parent's ℤ form) lets the injectivity contradictions be discharged by `omega`-driven substitution with no cast bookkeeping.
mathContext: Left: $\frac{num}{den}<\frac{la+ra}{lb+rb}$. Right: $\frac{la+ra}{lb+rb}<\frac{num}{den}$, both cross-multiplied to avoid division.

title: From State Injectivity to Value Injectivity
content: The parent proved that different paths give different 4-tuple STATES; a bijection of rationals needs different paths to give different VALUES. `mediant_inj_gen` closes this gap by induction: same-direction prefixes recurse; opposite directions place the two nodes on opposite sides of the mediant (via the BST bounds), so equal values are impossible; a `nil` path sits exactly at the mediant, again contradicting a strictly-displaced subtree node. `toRat_injective` then uses per-node coprimality (`coprime_path`) to recover `(num,den)` from the rational, yielding `Function.Injective toRat`.
mathContext: Equal reduced fractions $\frac{n_1}{d_1}=\frac{n_2}{d_2}$ with $\gcd(n_i,d_i)=1$ force $n_1=n_2,\ d_1=d_2$ (via $n_1\mid n_2$ and $n_2\mid n_1$).

title: The Stern-Brocot Bijection paths ≃ ℚ⁺
content: `sternBrocot_bijection` is the capstone: `toRat` is injective and `Set.range toRat = {x : ℚ | 0 < x}`. Range inclusion `⊆` is the parent's `toRat_pos`; `⊇` is the surjectivity just proved. Together with injectivity this is a genuine bijection between binary left/right paths and the positive rationals — a constructive, duplicate-free enumeration in which every rational appears exactly once and already in lowest terms, using only the foundational axioms (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`).
mathContext: $\text{toRat}:\text{Path}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb{Q}^{+}$, injective with range $\{x:0<x\}$. No Cantor pairing, no reduction step.

title: Concrete Surjectivity Witnesses
content: Three existence checks instantiate `reach_root`: the paths encoding `2/3`, `3/2`, and the larger coprime pair `22/7` all exist, with coprimality discharged by `decide`. These confirm the engine on small inputs (matching the parent's level-2 examples) and on a value whose path is long enough to exhibit the continued-fraction structure.
